description: The side whose changes determine database relationship updates: @ManyToOne owns a bidirectional one-to-many, while either side may own a bidirectional many-to-many.
The attribute that marks the inverse side of a bidirectional association by naming the field on the owning side.
A setting that passes persist, merge, remove, refresh or detach from a parent entity to the entities in its association.
A setting on one-to-many and one-to-one that deletes a child when it is removed from the parent's collection, applied at flush.
The choice between EAGER and LAZY loading of an association, where to-one defaults to eager and to-many defaults to lazy.
The extra table that stores pairs of keys for a many-to-many association, mapped with @JoinTable or as a link entity.
A stable natural value such as a tag name that an entity can use in equals and hashCode instead of its generated id.
